# nanobot: thirty wrong answers to track down without a test suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits, and the fallout shows up all over ordinary use.

This program runs assistants that talk to model providers and to outside helper services on a user's behalf, and it now gets a great deal wrong in ordinary use. Nothing about the protocols changed and nothing about the callers changed: the same invocations that used to be handled correctly are now handled wrongly, and in many places something that used to succeed now comes back as a flat error.

Getting the program started with its own settings is the first thing that goes wrong. Handing it two settings files in order no longer works at all: rather than the second file overriding the first one's assistant name while keeping the earlier instructions, adding its own extra assistant and concatenating the two top-level entry name lists, the whole thing comes back as a failure with nothing produced. The assistant that ships bundled with the program is still brought in and still carries its instructions, but the description written in its header block arrives empty. Pointing the program at a folder of definition documents in which one file explicitly marks itself as the default also comes out wrong — the two definitions in that folder no longer both turn up under their own names with both of them present in the list of top-level entries.
